title: Routing telemetry: compact per-request verdict snapshots and tier-sensitive metrics
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description:
Problem: Smart routing decisions (region selection, tier routing, and model-variant fallback) are currently opaque in our traces. Engineers need fast, low-cost visibility per request to debug incorrect routing, attribute latency/cost to specific routing legs, and verify fallback behavior without pulling huge trace payloads.

Goal: Ship a compact per-request 'verdict snapshot' format and per-tier counters so that every routed request can be repro-sampled and aggregated for SLO checks. The snapshot must be small (<= 1KB typical), include a stable routing rationale hash, tier attribution, latency budget used, and the minimal provenance needed to reconstruct the route in replay systems.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change routing policy rules or add new fallback strategies. It also does not replace full distributed tracing for deep perf dives; instead it complements traces with a lightweight, queryable layer focused on routing outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: A compact verdict snapshot schema is defined and documented in Confluence (<=1KB typical payload).
API and runtime attach a verdict snapshot to 100% of routed requests in prod (sampling exceptions documented).
Console UI exposes per-tier aggregated metrics and a searchable index of verdict hashes with links to traces/recorded replays.
End-to-end test that simulates a three-hop routing chain (edge -> region -> fallback) and verifies snapshots reconstruct the chain with correct latency attribution.
Storage cost estimate validated: 30-day retention for all verdicts at 10M req/day must cost <15% of current observability budget (proof in PR).
tasks: Design schema for compact verdict snapshot and publish Confluence doc: include fields: timestamp, request_id, verdict_hash, selected_region, tier, model_variant, reason_codes, latency_ms, kb_cache_hit, sampling_flag, trace_id_ref.
Implement encoder/decoder in runtime (C++) with configurable sampling and size guardrails.
Add server-side ingestion pipeline: Kafka topic, compact serializer, and materialized view in ClickHouse for rollups.
Wire Console: per-tier rollup panels and a lookup by verdict_hash that links into the trace and replay recorder.
Add E2E test harness in integration suite to validate snapshot fidelity and size limits.
Perf run to measure encoder CPU and end-to-end p95 latency impact; introduce opt-out policy for ultra-low-latency tiers if needed.

design_notes: Schema trade-offs: full trace embedding vs. compact snapshot. We opted for compact snapshots with a stable hash (verdict_hash) so heavy queries can join on the hash to fetch full traces on demand. To keep size down we intern region/tier/model strings and use small reason-code enums. Sampling policy: deterministic by customer_id mod 100 to maintain cross-request reproducibility. Storage: write a Kafka compacted topic for recent snapshots and a ClickHouse hourly materialized view for aggregated per-tier counters.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): schema and runtime encoder + 10% deterministic sampling, Kafka topic, minimal ClickHouse table for rollups. Phase 2 (1 sprint): Console integration and search by verdict_hash, rollout to 100% for non-latency-critical tiers. Phase 3 (adopt): evaluate retention and cost, tune sampling/retention to meet budget.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Observability costs spike if sampling misconfigured. Mitigation: default 10% deterministic sampling and enforced size limits. Risk: Sensitive data in payload. Mitigation: encoder explicitly forbids prompt text and any user PII; security sign-off required for any schema change. Risk: Increased p95 latency for ultra-low-latency tiers. Mitigation: opt-out flag per tenant/tier in routing config.
